newsitem.title: UK: UK Major's office plays down election speculation.
newsitem.headline: UK Major's office plays down election speculation.

text.p: Senior officials from British Prime Minister John Major's office on Thursday played down speculation of an imminent election announcement.

"I'm not expecting a press conference," one senior official said when asked about any election news. He added he was not anticipating that the weekly cabinet meeting would have a political discussion after ending regular government business.
The officials shrugged off questions on whether Major planned to see head of state Queen Elizabeth on Thursday, saying the prime minister had had a routine meeting with the queen on Tuesday.
Major would have to go to the queen to ask for parliament to be dissolved in order to hold the election.

The official declined to give any hint of when an election might be held, saying "I'm not going to rule out an election statement. When an election statement is to be made by the prime minister, I will tell you at the time."
An election must be held by May 22 and May 1 is Major's preferred date.
